analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. Per the patch, the only change is three new rows at head lines ~1751-1753, in the table of environment variables forwarded to the launchd daemon: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS. Those lines are outside the supplied excerpts, which cover head lines 1-830, so I examined only the patch hunk and the surrounding visible documentation. No source code, defaults or security controls are changed.

The new variables sound memory- or latency-related (idle cache sweep, segment retention, host zeros). They touch the GPU/KV-cache residue area (T-028) and possibly the TTFT oracle (T-041). Their effects are not described in the supplied text. If the variable named DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION or the idle sweep changes how long decrypted KV data stays resident, or how cache hits behave, the threat model may need an update for T-028 or T-041. That cannot be determined from a docs-only table row. The implementing files are GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift and EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, and the next pass should check them if they are in the PR. It should also check that forwarding these variables into launchd does not bypass the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate or the 30-minute TTL.

The visible portions of the doc are consistent with the threat model. Logout revokes only with HTTP 204 as confirmation. GLM encrypted SSD prefix cache defaults on, with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the opt-out. The cache storage statements match T-041. No regression was identified from the supplied evidence.
